text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The new road tax will become effective starting August 1, despite protests by drivers' trade unions which threatened to block traffic on roads across the country.
- The government decided to increase child allowances to up to 100,000 lei for families with more than four children.
- Wheat harvesting in the western Timis county was slowed down by rain.
- The Dacia Pitesti SA car maker, Galati shipyard and two commercial banks will be listed on the Bucharest stock exchange soon, the paper said.
- A shareholders' meeting at the private Columna bank decided to appoint a new board.
- Workers in the railway sector support the new road tax.
- A group of U.S. companies plan to invest one billion dollars in Romania's energy sector.
- The RAFO SA refinery in Onesti asked local authorities to issue a letter of guarantee for a $7 million credit to buy crude oil.
- Prices in food shops are still high despite recent cuts in import taxes, the paper says.
- Senator Trita Fanita asked the agriculture ministry to set at 1,000 lei per kilograme the purchasing price for the wheat harvested this year.
